trig-ratio.def: A ratio of two sides of a right triangle, named from an acute angle $\theta$: $\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, $\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$ (SOH CAH TOA). It depends only on the angle, not on the size of the triangle.

hypotenuse.def: The side of a right triangle across from the right angle, and its longest side. The other two sides, the legs, are named from an acute angle $\theta$: the opposite side is across from $\theta$, the adjacent side touches $\theta$.
